bull.b: The substantial cash balance and projected runway into Q3 2028 give Wave time to advance several clinical programs without immediate financing pressure. This supports continuity of research investment and provides flexibility while regulatory and partnering milestones develop.

Wave is advancing multiple assets across obesity, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, and liver disease, reducing reliance on a single clinical opportunity. Progress into mid-stage trials and toward a CTA creates several potential value inflection points over the coming quarters.

The proprietary chemistry and modality strategy could provide a durable competitive foundation if the claimed potency and durability advantages translate clinically. A differentiated platform may support repeated internal discoveries, broader pipeline productivity, and future partnering opportunities.

bear.b: Large recurring cash outflows mean Wave must convert pipeline progress into collaboration receipts, milestones, financing, or eventual product revenue to sustain operations. Continued burn can reduce financial flexibility over time and increase dependence on capital or partner funding.

The sharp decline in collaboration revenue highlights the variability of Wave’s current funding model and its exposure to partner-related payment timing. Until recurring product revenue exists, weaker collaboration receipts can amplify losses and make financial performance less predictable.

Wave’s future growth depends on clinical readouts, regulatory requirements, and partnership execution that remain unresolved. Delays or unfavorable outcomes could postpone commercialization, alter development plans, and extend the period before the pipeline can generate durable operating revenue.
